**The Fact:** The Moon is actually **tidally locked** to Earth, meaning it rotates on its axis at exactly the same speed that it orbits our planet.

**Why It Matters:**
This phenomenon explains why we only ever see one side of the Moon from Earth (the "nearside"). Because the rotation period matches the orbital period, the Moon completes one spin in the time it takes to complete one orbit around us.

If the Moon rotated faster or slower than it orbited, we would see different portions of its surface over the course of a month. This tidal locking has also played a crucial role in Earth's history; the gravitational pull of the Moon stabilizes Earth's axial tilt (obliquity). Without this stabilization, Earth's climate could swing wildly between ice ages and hot periods, making life as we know it much harder to sustain.
